title: Rapid Runway: Seller Runbook & Execution Snippets (Sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This sketch is a compact, operational slide deck and runbook for sellers and SEs to practice a 10–15 minute technical + economics pitch and a 3-minute rapid demo. It is intentionally lean — designed for live roleplay, quick rehearsals before discovery calls, and as a script for small pilots.

When to use:
- Pre-call warmup for any technical demo where latency, cost, or reliability are top buyer concerns
- Pilot kickoffs with platform/infra teams and integration architects
- Rapid escalation lanes when a prospect asks about resilience or on-prem options

Primary audience:
- Field SEs, Platform Sellers, Solutions Engineers, AE technical leads

How to run this in 20 minutes:
1) 5 min: TL;DR + positioning + 1-minute architecture sketch
2) 7 min: Live demo (generate/chat + routing fallback example) with narrated economics
3) 5 min: Pilot checklist, success criteria, next steps + Q/A
4) 3 min: Close with immediate pilot ask (trial, embed test, or POC scope)

Slide-by-slide outline (speaker cues included):
- Slide 1 — 30s TL;DR: "Why Redwood matters for inference at scale"
  Speaker cue: 30s one-liner, highlight predictable unit costs and production-ready fallbacks
- Slide 2 — 1m Problem frame: "Most infra costs and surprises come at inference, not training"
  Cue: cite quick stat "70% of token spend is avoidable with caching/batching" (example metric).
- Slide 3 — 90s Architecture sketch: hosted vs dedicated vs private (single graphic)
  Cue: point to same API, different control/SLAs — emphasize migration path
- Slide 4 — 2m Runtime differentiators: batching, KV cache, quant-friendly kernels
  Cue: three bullet tech wins and expected real-world impact (latency down, ops load down)
- Slide 5 — 2m Fallbacks & routing policy example (scenario walkthrough)
  Demo cue: show fallback from high-capacity variant to a cheaper compatible model with no consumer-facing outage (scripted log lines)
- Slide 6 — 3m Economics snippet: per-token example, reserved vs burst pricing, unit math for a feature
  Cue: run a micro-calculation for a chat feature at 5k users / 2 requests per user / avg 40 tokens generated
- Slide 7 — 3–5m Live demo script (timed):
  Demo steps (SE reads):
    1. Start with a short prompt: "Summarize user message and suggest next action"
    2. Show real-time streaming response, note observed latency
    3. Trigger a simulated capacity constraint, show automatic fallback to variant B
    4. Observe identical structured output; call out slight quality delta and cost drop
  Cue: keep it deterministic — use canned prompt set in the demo repo
- Slide 8 — 1m Rehearsal checklist (pre-call):
  - Confirm demo project is seeded with credentials
  - Confirm region matches prospect's preferred region
  - Confirm token budget for demo (avoid long hallucination tails)
- Slide 9 — 2m Pilot scope and success criteria
  - Pilot goals: latency <= 250ms p95 for user-facing flows, >80% request coverage by cache/batching
  - Success metrics: cost per successful response, % fallbacks invoked, error rate
- Slide 10 — 1m Next steps & ask: pilot template, sample contract language, SE handoff checklist

Seller rapid scripts (snackable lines):
- Opening value line: "Most customers expect modern LLMs to be magical — the operational load after launch is where teams get surprised. Redwood is the runtime and guardrail that makes inference predictable."
- When asked "Why not run ourselves?": "We partner with teams that want to control models, not manage all of the ops plumbing — we keep the controls in your hands while removing the heavy lifting of day-to-day inference ops."
- If buyer asks about on-prem: "We offer a private control plane option so you can keep data and key material inside your VPC or air-gapped environment and still benefit from the same rollout tooling."

Common objections and short counters (30–45s each):
- "We’re concerned about vendor lock-in": "We expose standard APIs and model artifacts; customers keep full portability and can run compatible weights in their environment — the value is in the management + run-time optimizations we provide."
- "We can’t accept inconsistent latency": "We support reserved pools with SLAs and automatic local fallbacks; if latency is critical we can include regional capacity and warm cache agreements in the pilot."
- "Cost is lower if we batch ourselves": "Batching is subtle and workload-dependent; we automatically tune it and provide transparent simulations for expected unit economics so you can validate before committing."

Roleplay prompts for practice (SE/AE exercise):
- Play A (SE): Lead the architecture sketch and demo fallback.
- Play B (Buyer): Ask about procurement and security (probe for KMS/HSM and audit logs).
- Goal: Close to a pilot ask in 2 minutes after the demo.

Demo checklist (pre-demo):
- Demo service account configured and not throttled
- Demo dataset is sanitized and < 10k tokens total for run
- Fallback toggle script available and tested locally
- Visuals: console traces & cost chart ready to switch to during call

Pilot template (starter scope, copyable snippet for follow-up email):
"Proposed pilot: 4 weeks, dedicated test pool, ingest 50k inference requests, success criteria: p95 latency < 250ms; fallback rate < 10%; cost per 1K responses reduced by 30% vs baseline. Redwood will provide SE time for integration and a weekly sync for the pilot."

Metrics to surface during pilot reviews:
- p50/p95 latency for critical route
- tokens generated per request and per customer cohort
- fallback invocation rate and fallback latency delta
- estimated $/1k responses and projected annualized delta

Appendix — quick links and artifacts to prep the call:
- demo repo with canned prompts (github: repo/quick-demo-pr-412)
- pilot contract template (confluence:GF-1423-runbook-ops)
- example SLO language and reserved pool spec (JIRA:GTMPILOT-78)

Notes for SEs: keep the demo focused on buyer outcomes (latency, reliability, cost predictability). Avoid deep kernel-level claims in early calls; use observable metrics and concrete pilot commitments.

Version note: This is an early sketch intended to be refactored into a compact 8-slide deck and a 1-page one-pager for AEs. Feedback requested: which objections did you hit most often on recent calls? Add to the appendix for the next pass.
